subject: Incremental output guarantees — request for SLA wording and variance
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@lumenpay.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify delivery guarantees for streaming vs sync endpoints

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week — our engineering team liked the latency profile. Procurement asked me to get explicit SLA language for two delivery modes we plan to use: a streaming chat endpoint (live output to user) and a non-streaming/batched endpoint (background summarization jobs). They want concrete commitments for time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained token/sec expectations under the Dedicated plan, plus any fallback behavior if streaming pools are saturated.

Specific asks from our side:
- TTFT target for 95th percentile under normal load and under scaled burst conditions
- Sustained tokens/sec per connection and per-tenant limits
- What happens if streaming capacity is exhausted (will requests fall back to non-streaming with different guarantees?)
- Any unit cost or billing differences for streaming vs non-streaming when fallbacks occur

We need this language by early next week to include in our procurement SOW. Can you share a proposed amendment or matrix we can review?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Product, LumenPay
(attachment: example_slo_requests.pdf - pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@lumenpay.com>
Cc: Tim O'Neill <tim@lumenpay.com>
Date: 2028-06-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify delivery guarantees for streaming vs sync endpoints

On Tue, Jun 25, 2028 at 09:12 AM Sarah Lin <sarah@lumenpay.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo last week — our engineering team liked the latency profile.
> Specific asks from our side: TTFT target for 95th percentile...

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a short impact matrix and a suggested amendment to the Hosted/Dedicated SOW that spells out streaming vs batch delivery commitments. High level summary below:

- Proposed 95th-percentile TTFT for streaming: 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), 250ms for long prompts (>=512 tokens) under normal Dedicated capacity.
- Burst scenario (temporary overcommit): we offer a prioritized streaming pool for paid Dedicated customers; if that pool is saturated we will either: 1) route to a warm fallback pool (best-effort streaming, TTFT + 100–300ms) or 2) degrade to non-streaming synchronous endpoint with guaranteed completion latency bounds (TTT - time-to-complete defined) and token/sec profiles.
- Sustained throughput guidance: recommend target of 30–60 tokens/sec per concurrent streaming connection for typical LLMs; non-streaming batch jobs should use chunked requests and are billed per output token with higher sustained throughput per-job.

I attached: SLA_impact_matrix.xlsx (breakout by prompt size & traffic shape) and scope_amendment_LumenPay_v1.docx (draft wording).

Next steps — if this looks reasonable I can flag as an exception request internally to lock in the prioritized streaming pool and the fallback wording for your SOW. If procurement wants hard numeric failure modes, we should set an acceptance test (synthetic workload) and an agreed ramp for burst capacity.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(attachment: SLA_impact_matrix.xlsx - spreadsheet)(attachment: scope_amendment_LumenPay_v1.docx - docx)

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@lumenpay.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@lumenpay.com, Tim O'Neill <tim@lumenpay.com>
Date: 2028-06-28T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify delivery guarantees for streaming vs sync endpoints

Jordan — this is really helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups from procurement and our infra lead:

- Procurement would like the streaming TTFT numbers expressed in the SOW as two tiers (standard and guaranteed) with credits tied to the guaranteed tier. Can you propose credit thresholds?
- Our infra lead asked for the explicit fallback ordering and whether payloads are retried automatically or if the client must reissue the request when we fall back to sync mode.
- We also need a short clause that the prioritized streaming pool remains available for the duration of the contract at the committed capacity, with an agreed ramp schedule for increases.

Can you circulate a one-page amendment that includes: the numeric TTFT commitments, sustained token/sec guidance, fallback semantics (auto-retry vs explicit client retry), billing implications when fallback is used, and the test plan for acceptance? If you can get that to procurement by Wednesday we can keep the procurement timeline.

Thanks — looping procurement so they have the draft.

Cheers,
Sarah
(attachment: procurement_requirements.csv - csv)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-30T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify delivery guarantees for streaming vs sync endpoints — LumenPay amendment request

Team — forwarding LumenPay's procurement asks (see thread below). We need an internal decision & sign-off to propose a final one-page amendment by Wed (2028-07-03). Quick summary of what they're asking and my recommended positions:

1) Numeric TTFT commitments (95th percentile):
   - Proposed STANDARD: 95th TTFT = 250ms (<=128 tokens), 400ms (>=512 tokens)
   - Proposed GUARANTEED (paid dedicated pool + exception): 95th TTFT = 120ms (<=128 tokens), 250ms (>=512 tokens) with SLA credits if breached

2) Sustained throughput guidance:
   - Recommend we commit to a guideline of 40 tokens/sec per concurrent streaming connection for typical conversational models. For higher sustained throughput we should recommend a dedicated concurrency license (additional capacity).

3) Fallback semantics and client behavior:
   - Preference: automatic graceful fallback to a best-effort streaming pool for short retries (no client action). If that fails, degrade to a non-streaming synchronous path but only after we have attempted up to 1 automatic failover. On degrade to sync the client will receive a definitive completion response; we will not silently drop the request.
   - Billing: When fallback to sync occurs, billing will be at the non-streaming per-output-token rate; if the fallback was due to Redwood capacity constraints we offer a partial credit offset (TBD).

4) Test plan / acceptance criteria:
   - Agreed synthetic acceptance test: 10k requests at target concurrency for 30 minutes, measuring 95th TTFT and sustained token/sec. Failure & remediation thresholds to be defined in the amendment.

Attachments: I propose we attach SLA_impact_matrix.xlsx and our internal fallback policy (redwood-streaming-fallback-policy.pdf) to the amendment.

Ask: Marissa — can you approve committing to GUARANTEED tier for LumenPay as an exception (we'd convert to a reserved capacity deal)? Karthik — can you confirm the feasibility of 120ms 95th TTFT at scale for their projected concurrency and whether the automatic one-attempt failover is realistic operationally? Grace — if we accept guaranteed TTFT, what does this imply for onboarding/CS support and runbook requirements?

I can draft the one-pager once you give thumbs up on the above.

Thanks,
Jordan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-streaming-fallback-policy.pdf - pdf)
